blocking.finding: A human approval delivered before register_gate is lost and the architect parks forever: the reducer ignores artifact.approved for a document no gate names yet (spec Errors row), handleGatesRegister records the document as unapproved without reading Dispatch, and dispatch_request_approval on an already-approved document returns 200 with ask null and emits no event (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/reviews.go requestArtifactApproval), so no artifact.approved ever arrives for that version. Reached by a header approval before the request, or an Inbox answer during the model turn between dispatch_request_approval and register_gate. Pre-existing in the ask gate (not a regression) but the one path where a human approval never opens the gate.
blocking.remedy: When the gate computed in handleGatesRegister is not open, read the issue once via ctx.deps.dispatchClient.getIssue(issue) (the read specArtifactResolver already uses); find artifacts[].id === artifactId; if approval.state === "approved" and approval.version === approval.latest_version, set latestVersion = max(latestVersion, latest_version) and approvedVersion = approval.version, then publish design-approved through publishDesignApproved exactly as the gates.design: off branch does (one shared closed-to-open wake path). A failed read fails the registration with 502 so the architect retries rather than register a gate that silently cannot open. Add api.test.ts cases (Dispatch reports approved at the registered version -> gate open, exactly one wake; reports awaiting -> unchanged). Update the packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md sentence that says the migration is the only Dispatch read outside resync.ts. Reordering the skill (register before request) closes only the Inbox window, not the header-approval one, so it is not a substitute. Humans still write every approval; the daemon only reads what a human already wrote — inside the no-agent-path ruling.

nonBlocking.finding: The already-approved branch (result.ask === null) text names only the file; state the document id the way the approval-requested text now does — it is the branch the blocking finding sends the architect through.
artifactId is stored in the architect letter case; Dispatch emits lowercase and gateFor compares with ===. Lowercase at register (or compare case-insensitively).
Hand-rolled positive-integer check duplicates the contract (already enforced before the handler) and the existing requiredNumber helper; the 400 is unreachable.

Migrated state is not saved at load; until the first ordinary save each restart re-reads every kept gate from Dispatch and re-depends on Dispatch at boot. Save once when sourceVersion < validatedState.version.
checkpoint_three switches on $design_gate twice in a row; merge the second case into the first.
The which-phase-worker-on-the-root jq is pasted in tree_progress and checkpoint_four with two phrasings; one helper. Same family: the released-status set is spelled two ways.
Second, looser definition of a Dispatch artifact id beside the contract z.uuid(); an id can pass the tool and still 400 at the daemon (named field, so not silent).

Shapes confirmed against server.go versionEventPayload and model.ArtifactReviewEventPayload.

Reducers pure and synchronous; approval below latestVersion recorded, closed, no wake; duplicate approval at the recorded version a no-op past the seq fence; changes_requested deletes approvedVersion, raises latestVersion, wakes {type, version, reason, author?}; artifact.version raises silently; lastAppliedSeq stamped for all three whether or not a gate matched; ask.answered no longer switched on. Tests fed the contract JSON fixtures verbatim.

observations: The production pi-legion-envoy plugin in this pane prepends N `export LEGION_GRANT=` lines to each bash call, N growing over the session (1 at start, 4 by the twentieth call); only one of the minted grants redeems, and it is not the last one exported, so a plain `legion gh` fails with `Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT (403)` on most calls. Worked around with a DEBUG trap that records every exported grant and retries `legion gh` with each. Worth its own issue for the plugin (this branch legion.ts already moves the grant to the tool env instead of command text).

The Legion daemon at 127.0.0.1:13370 refused connections twice (about two minutes, then about 100 s) at 03:5x-04:0x UTC while this review ran; every bash call was blocked with `Unable to connect` until it returned on its own at state version 24.
